evals.prompt: My markata-go site has both posts and docs. I want docs pages under `/docs/` to use a docs-style layout with a left sidebar and right table of contents, but I do not want to rewrite all templates. What config should I change and what should it look like?
evals.expected_output: Explains that layout config is the right first step, points to `[markata-go.layout]` and `[markata-go.layout.paths]`, and gives a concrete TOML example instead of jumping straight to plugin or full template work.

evals.prompt: Please create a new post about my release notes for version 0.8. I want frontmatter that works well with markata-go, includes tags and description, and keeps me from forgetting the publish date.
evals.expected_output: Uses `markata-go new` or current frontmatter conventions, produces practical starter frontmatter, and keeps the guidance focused on content/frontmatter rather than template or plugin changes.

evals.prompt: On my markata-go blog I want feed cards to show the description under the title and use a compact byline. I already have a `templates/` folder. Which file should I inspect first and how would you make the smallest safe change?
evals.expected_output: Steers the answer toward the smallest relevant template or partial, preserves existing site conventions, and avoids rebuilding the whole template tree.

evals.prompt: My production deploy on GitHub Pages builds, but the feed URLs and some absolute asset URLs still point at localhost. How should I debug this in a markata-go site repo and what config or env values are most likely wrong?
evals.expected_output: Focuses on `url`, environment overrides such as `MARKATA_GO_URL`, and build/deploy validation steps before suggesting template rewrites.

evals.prompt: I want each post page to show a small computed reading estimate and a badge when it links to a GitHub repo. Should this live in frontmatter, config, templates, or a plugin? Please reason through the options for a normal markata-go site repo.
evals.expected_output: Explains the config/content/template/plugin decision clearly, prefers lower-cost options first, and only recommends plugin work when the behavior cannot be expressed with existing fields, templates, or built-in features.

evals.prompt: Please create an `analytics.md` page for my markata-go site. I want KPI callouts, a chart of publishing activity, and a topic-mix section, but I want to write the timeline story in my own voice. Use built-in stats or chart features when possible and leave me good prompts where I should add interpretation.
evals.expected_output: Creates or recommends a Jinja-enabled analytics page pattern, uses built-in stats and chart features instead of inventing a plugin, includes concrete metrics/chart structure, and leaves clear author-facing prompts for the narrative sections.

evals.prompt: On my markata-go site I want feed cards and post pages to show word count and reading time, and I also want an about page to show total posts and total reading time for the whole site. What template fields should I use and what is the smallest safe change?
evals.expected_output: Points to `post.Extra.word_count`, `post.Extra.reading_time_text`, and `config.Extra.site_stats` fields, keeps the change in templates or partials, and avoids suggesting unnecessary plugin work.

evals.prompt: I want an analytics page on my markata-go second brain that highlights orphan notes, the most-linked notes, and a simple publishing cadence chart. Please stay within built-in data the site already has and tell me what belongs in Jinja markdown versus external analytics.
evals.expected_output: Uses built-in or derivable build-side data such as `inlinks`, `outlinks`, post dates, and existing stats fields, clearly separates build-derived analytics from external traffic analytics, and gives a practical `analytics.md` structure for orphan-note and link-graph storytelling.

evals.prompt: On my markata-go site I want to add Web Awesome tabs and tooltips to my docs. Should I do this in config, markdown content, templates, or a plugin, and what should I inspect first before editing?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the first checks are existing `hooks`, `webawesome` config, current `wa-*` usage, and template wiring; prefers enabling the built-in `webawesome` hook plus markdown containers or raw `wa-*` HTML before suggesting plugin work; mentions vendor versus CDN asset behavior and avoiding duplicate hardcoded includes.

evals.prompt: I am outside my work-notes repository. Find the note about incident review, update it, and create a follow-up note without changing my current directory.
evals.expected_output: Uses `--site-dir` or `MARKATA_GO_SITE_DIR`, searches with path output, explains that the returned absolute Markdown path can be edited directly, creates the follow-up with `new --no-input`, and validates with lint or a fast build.

evals.prompt: Add a product roadmap to my about page that shows our quarterly milestones and draws itself as the reader scrolls. Each milestone links to its announcement post.
evals.expected_output: Uses a built-in `::: road timeline` container (or another suitable road style) with one `- [Title](url) Label` item per milestone, closes it with a colon-only line, and does not create a custom template, JavaScript file, or config change. Validates with a fast build.

evals.prompt: My Markata post should be a visual feature roadmap: a rocket line icon in a rounded square next to 'Verify production', and two centered server/database icons above Falcon2 and Falcon3 cards. Can you author this in Markdown? Make sure it works on mobile and without JS.
evals.expected_output: Uses existing :lucide-rocket:, :lucide-server:, :lucide-database: Markdown shortcodes plus md-feature/md-feature-icon/md-feature-body and md-columns/md-card/md-icon containers with colon-depth-matched closers. Keeps visible text headings, uses the built-in pinned/local icons plugin and CSS-only layouts, and avoids inventing an SVG library, CDN, icon font, or plugin. Mentions local/cached icon requirement for first offline build and validates the generated page.

evals.prompt: I'm a Codex agent editing a Markata site. The user wants modern icons and metrics cards. Is this a Web Awesome dependency? What bundled skill topic and docs should I read? How do I update stale installed agent instructions?
evals.expected_output: Reads topics/rich-markdown.md in bundled markata-go-site skill, distinguishes built-in :lucide-name: inline SVG from Web Awesome, uses existing md-* containers and metrics. Points to docs/guides/icons.md and docs/guides/markdown-containers.md; tells user to run markata agent update and markata agent doctor after installing an updated binary, rather than claiming committed docs automatically update previously installed skills.

evals.prompt: Create a visual post on my Markata site showing release readiness. I want a small dashboard: passing checks, what is not deployed, a progress indicator, a short evidence table and a clear next-action handoff. Use known results; do not invent percentages.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes generic visual-post/dashboard intent and uses topics/visual-authoring.md; composes a static-first status/metric layout with md-status, md-stat, md-progress only with known numerator/denominator, and an accessible evidence table. Explicitly separates code merged, CI passed, deployed and verified live. Uses native Markata primitives, no proprietary UI syntax or fabricated values.

evals.prompt: Visualize how our small app is deployed: builder produces the site, server serves it, and a shared volume connects them. I'd like a diagram readers can understand on phones with JavaScript off.
evals.expected_output: Selects an md-layout/md-box/md-columns/md-connector topology when it is sufficient, uses descriptive accessible text and responsive theme tokens, or a Mermaid flowchart only if arbitrary connections warrant it. Mentions Mermaid runtime compatibility and no-JavaScript fallback; does not install a frontend graph framework.

evals.prompt: Turn these measured monthly publishing totals into a simple dashboard and chart-driven article in my Markata site. Make it visual but accessible and keep raw data visible when scripts are disabled.
evals.expected_output: Uses existing chartjs fences with semantic build-time table fallback, a small clearly labeled KPI section, or contribution-graph for calendar-style activity when appropriate. Separates provided measurements from conjecture, validates Chart.js JSON and mobile/dark modes, and follows generic visualization intent rather than a platform-specific UI.

evals.prompt: I am in a small command-line project that is not itself a Markata site. Create one self-contained Markdown document using the $markata-go-site visual design skill to explain its workflow: discover items, choose which to keep or archive, safely apply changes, and verify. Keep it readable and not crowded.
evals.expected_output: Creates exactly one Markata-flavored Markdown file in the existing repository without site scaffolding. Uses clear unboxed article title/short lead, one main flow representation, a small number of real-choice cards, and calm prose for other steps. Does not duplicate each road milestone as a feature row or cram instructions into every card. Documents the relevant destructive-action caution, avoids fabricated metrics, and explains that visually styled rendering requires Markata.

evals.prompt: The visual guide you wrote works, but it feels dense: a road of five steps, then five icon feature rows repeating those steps, plus multiple card grids and tightly packed H3 headings. Please improve the design's breathing room and typographic rhythm without removing needed information.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes repetition and small-card density as the defects without equating breathing room with eliminating helpful visuals. Preserves an orientation/overview, a road for sequence, distinct decision or side-route cards where useful, and quieter explanatory prose; trims repeated descriptions and improves spacing and heading hierarchy. Compares previous and new renders and does not invent metrics or claim an unperformed browser preview.

evals.prompt: Draw one exact dependency graph for my Markata article, including complex cross-links. I specifically want just a Mermaid diagram and a short accessibility explanation.
evals.expected_output: Respects the explicitly narrow single-diagram request: uses a Mermaid fenced diagram with runtime-supported syntax and nearby accessible text, without forcing a dashboard, icon card collection or unrelated visual components. Distinguishes one requested graph from a broadly requested visual post.

evals.prompt: Design a long-form, calm, accessible visual report. I care about hierarchy and whitespace more than quantity of widgets. Explain how to treat heading sizes and nested Markata containers, including a comparison that needs two cards.
evals.expected_output: Leads with a single visible title and concise deck (avoids duplicate frontmatter/template H1), keeps semantic H2 headings prominent, distinguishes contained heading sizes and weights supported by the current theme, and uses meaningful comparison cards separated from explanatory text. Relies on the system font default without custom fonts or arbitrary palette colors. Tests actual spacing/mobile wrapping when possible; uses visual variety rather than either all cards or all prose.

evals.prompt: I asked an agent to make a visual document. Version A has two orientation cards, a five-step road, readable icon-assisted explanations, decision cards, and side-route cards. The copy in cards is a bit dense. Version B has more blank space but removes the opening visual and side routes, leaving a road and a long plain numbered explanation. The second feels worse. Improve the document without inventing facts or making it complicated.
evals.expected_output: Treats Version B as a visual-design regression despite improved whitespace. Preserves the useful visual orientation and decision/side-route groupings that make Version A skimmable; shortens card copy and moves detailed instructions into prose, adds separation between visual groups, improves hierarchy and label sizes, and retains road as wayfinding without duplicating identical feature content. Does not enforce exact card quotas, introduce unrelated widgets, or simply restore every dense detail.

evals.prompt: Make a visual Markdown article for a Markata site. The frontmatter title is shown in the template header. The source includes an identical '# Title' at the start of the body, so it renders twice. Please improve the visual page with an overview, process, and key decision.
evals.expected_output: Avoids duplicate visible title by removing the redundant body H1 when the template already prints it, while keeping a compelling lead and prominent H2 sections. Uses distinct orientation, process and choice visual treatments without repeating content; maintains semantic headings and no-JS readability.

evals.prompt: Create a polished visual report from these monthly counts: Jan 4, Feb 6, Mar 3, Apr 8. I want it to feel like a chart-driven article, with the right graph and a small explanation. Use built-in Markata Markdown and don't make up values.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a true Chart.js `line` fenced JSON block (not Mermaid, a Markdown table alone, or unsupported chat-chart syntax); labels months in order, uses exactly supplied values with series units, a visible chart heading and brief grounded interpretation. Includes standard aligned label/data arrays for Markata's no-JS data table; adds small optional md-stat/card overview without crowding the chart, and does not pretend theme-aware canvas or browser validation without evidence.

evals.prompt: Show a clean bar chart comparing these categories and counts: Docs 12, Tests 18, Fixes 9. Give the chart enough room and make it accessible on mobile with JavaScript disabled.
evals.expected_output: Creates a fenced `chartjs` JSON bar chart with explicit labels, numeric dataset values, a quantitative axis beginning at zero, clear unit/period/caption, and an aligned semantic fallback table generated at build time. Avoids a tiny chart in a side-by-side narrow card, handcoded proprietary chat components, and unverifiable CSS palette claims; checks plugin setup, responsive axes and fallback behavior.

evals.prompt: Make a visual dashboard where one chart shows monthly trends and another shows category share. Use an area-style chart and a doughnut. Explain when those choices help and when a table is better.
evals.expected_output: Uses a Chart.js `line` dataset with `fill:true` for area and a `doughnut` chart for a small known whole, with correct JSON, labels, readable legends, units and coherent supplied or clearly illustrative values. Uses separate semantic sections and short text, avoids arbitrary duplicate graphs and inaccessible canvas-only explanations. Notes when precise rankings are better represented by bar charts or tables.

evals.prompt: I have an analytics page showing 130 posts, 700000 words, and 210 code blocks. Make one bar chart comparing these site totals.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that posts, words and code blocks are incompatible units, and declines the misleading shared-axis bar chart. Recommends md-stat KPIs or separate meaningful same-unit charts, preserves exact counts, and explains the visualization choice without fabricating measurements.

evals.prompt: Visualize this session. We fixed a cache bug, the targeted test passed, and the documentation review remains open. There is an existing Markata site here. Make the result available for me to read.
evals.expected_output: Reads topics/visualize-session.md, creates a composed visual Markdown post using only the supplied session evidence, distinguishes tested work from pending review, preserves publication flags, serves on loopback or reuses the correct site server, checks the exact post URL and its content, attempts browser opening, and reports the artifact, URL, browser result, and server handle. Does not publish or deploy.
expectations: The post uses native visual containers and distinguishes the passed targeted test from pending documentation review.
The workflow selects the correct site and plans a persistent loopback preview without changing publication flags.
The workflow checks the exact post URL and intended content before attempting browser opening.
The handoff includes the Markdown path, preview URL, browser-open result, and server handle or stop instruction.

evals.prompt: Visualize this: our release process is draft, review, approval. This Python repository is not a Markata site. I want to read the visual post in my browser, but keep preview configuration and generated output out of this repository.
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied process rather than unrelated session history, authors native visual Markdown, creates any required Markata preview scaffolding in an isolated temporary directory, starts a persistent loopback server without disturbing other services, checks the exact post URL and intended content, and attempts browser opening. Reports limitations accurately and retains the preview plus authored Markdown for the user.
expectations: The post uses native visual containers for the supplied draft, review, approval process.
The workflow keeps preview configuration, output, and cache outside the unrelated repository.
The workflow plans a persistent loopback preview and checks the exact post URL and intended content before opening it.
The handoff preserves the authored Markdown and preview while distinguishing planned actions from observed results.

evals.prompt: Make a visual post from this session: a cache fix passed its targeted test, but docs review is pending. Source only. Create exactly one Markdown file in this non-Markata repository. Do not serve it or open a browser.
evals.expected_output: Creates exactly one composed Markata Markdown artifact, separates tested work from pending review, and honors source-only scope. Does not create site configuration, preview scaffolding, generated output, a server, or a browser-open request. Explains that rich styling requires Markata.
expectations: The post uses native visual containers and distinguishes the passed targeted test from pending documentation review.
The workflow delivers exactly one Markdown artifact without site scaffolding, server startup, or browser opening.
The handoff explains that rich styling requires Markata and does not claim a browser preview occurred.
